court: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section)

facts.text: The applicant, Mr İsak Tepe, is a Turkish citizen born in 1943, living in İstanbul, and was the provincial chairman of the DEP in Bitlis in 1993.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  The applicant, Mr İsak Tepe, is a Turkish citizen who was born in 1943 and is at present living in İstanbul (Turkey). At the time of the events giving rise to his application, the applicant was the provincial chairman of a political party, the DEP (Democracy Party), in the province of Bitlis (south‑east Turkey).

facts.text: In early July 1993, General Korkmaz Tağma invited provincial political party leaders to a meeting at the army barracks; the applicant attended and spoke in support of Kurdish rights.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  In the beginning of July 1993, General Korkmaz Tağma, the commander of the Tatvan 6th Armoured Brigade, invited the provincial leaders of all political parties to a meeting at the army barracks. The applicant attended this meeting as the representative of the DEP and spoke in support of the cultural and democratic rights of the Kurdish population in Turkey.

facts.text: On 10 July 1993, the applicant's son, Ferhat Tepe, born in 1974 and working as a reporter, was taken into police custody and released the same day without reasons given.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  In the afternoon of 10 July 1993 the applicant’s son, Ferhat Tepe, born in 1974 and working as a reporter for the Özgür Gündem newspaper in Bitlis, was taken into police custody. No reasons were given for his arrest. He was released the same day in the afternoon.

facts.text: On 28 July 1993 at around 7 p.m., Ferhat was abducted in the schoolyard by a tall, bearded man known locally as a policeman, put in a car followed by a white Renault with registration 65 AD 095.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 28 July 1993 at around 7 p.m., while Ferhat was in the schoolyard of the Şemsi Bitlis primary school, a tall, bearded man who was known in the area to be a policeman, took him by the arm, put him in a car and drove away with him. Their car was followed by a white car, a Renault with the registration number 65 AD 095.

facts.text: On 29 July 1993 at around 6 a.m., the applicant received an anonymous phone call from a person claiming to be from the 'Ottoman Turkish Revenge Brigade' holding his son hostage and demanding closure of DEP's Bitlis branch, release of French tourists, and payment of one billion Turkish liras.

anchor.surface_text: 16.  On 29 July 1993 at around 6 a.m. the applicant received a phone call from an anonymous person who claimed to be a member of an organisation called the “Ottoman Turkish Revenge Brigade” and said that they were keeping his son as a hostage. The caller said that Ferhat would be killed unless the applicant closed down the DEP’s Bitlis branch, released four French tourists who were in the hands of the PKK and paid one billion Turkish liras (TRL).

facts.text: On 4 August 1993, Ferhat's dead body was found at Lake Hazar; the post-mortem concluded death by drowning with no signs of blows or force.

anchor.surface_text: 24.  Still on 4 August 1993, Ferhat’s dead body was found by a civil servant at the Lake Hazar, in Karakem. On the same day the public prosecutor and a medical expert examined the body. The report of their findings concluded that the cause of death was drowning and that there was no need for a systematic autopsy. It also stated that no signs of blows or the use of force on the body or of friction on the wrists and ankles had been detected.

facts.text: On 9 August 1993, the applicant identified Ferhat's exhumed body and observed crushed testicles, marks on arms, ankles, testicles, chest, cigarette burns, and deep wounds on wrists and ankles indicating binding and torture.

anchor.surface_text: 27.  On 9 August 1993 the applicant identified Ferhat’s body, which had been exhumed by the authorities. In preparation for the funeral ceremony, the applicant washed the body himself in a mosque. He saw that his son’s testicles had been crushed and that there were marks on the arms, ankles, testicles and chest. He observed some cigarette burn marks on the body but no fractures. There were also deep wounds on the wrists and ankles showing that Ferhat had been bound hand and foot.

facts.text: Following the funeral procession on 10 August 1993, police presence was strong; police filmed attendees, checked IDs, arrested fifteen persons, and searched the applicant's house.

anchor.surface_text: 29.  At the funeral procession in Bitlis on 10 August 1993, there was a strong police presence. The police filmed those who attended, checked their identification and arrested fifteen persons. Later on the same day the police searched the applicant’s house.

facts.text: The applicant and his family were under intense pressure from State authorities due to his political activities and investigation into his son's killing; family members were detained and tried on serious charges.

anchor.surface_text:
37.  Following the applicant’s complaints to the authorities, the police took tight security measures. The applicant, his office, his home and the DEP party building were put under constant surveillance. The police filmed the applicant’s colleagues and his fellow-townsmen who came to console him, and checked their identity cards.

37.  In the meantime, the applicant’s family had been under intense pressure from the State authorities in relation to his political activities, the investigation he had personally carried out into the killing of his son and his application to the European Commission of Human Rights. The applicant’s daughter was remanded in custody in December 1993; his son was remanded in custody in 1994 for four months and is currently being tried for an offence which carries the death sentence; another of the applicant’s daughters was taken into custody in April 1994; four of the applicant’s nephews were remanded in custody in 1994, one of whom is being tried for an offence which carries the death sentence; the applicant’s brother was taken into custody in April 1994 and the applicant’s cousin has been in Elazığ Prison since 1994. On 24 February 1996 the applicant was arrested in Bartın and held in police custody for eight days in Bitlis. During his detention, the police officers asked him why he accused the State and why he had taken his complaints to the European Commission. They further threatened him and said among other things: “We will kill you just as we killed Ferhat. You are complaining to the infidels about our State. Are they the ones who will save you? Well, let them come and save you.” After being released, the applicant was acquitted of the charges by the Diyarbakır State Security Court. On 4 March 1996 the applicant was allegedly taken into custody in Bitlis on charges of aiding the PKK. He was released on an unspecified date after being interrogated.

facts.text: In 1999, the applicant was arrested by anti-terrorist police while entering the HADEP party building in Istanbul, detained for one day, insulted and threatened with death by police officers.

anchor.surface_text: 39.  In 1999 the applicant was arrested by police officers from the anti-terrorist department while entering the HADEP (People’s Democracy Party) party building in the Kadıköy district in Istanbul. He was kept in detention for one day. The police officers insulted him and threatened him with death. One of the police officers said that they would kill him just as they had killed Ferhat. The applicant complained to the Fatih Public Prosecutor in Istanbul, who decided to discontinue the proceedings, as there was no witness to confirm his allegations.

facts.text: The Government submitted that Ferhat Tepe had been arrested twice in 1991 on suspicion of acting as a PKK courier.

anchor.surface_text: 40.  The applicant’s son Ferhat Tepe had been arrested on two occasions in 1991, as he was suspected of acting as a PKK courier.

facts.text: According to Government witnesses, on 28 July 1993 Ferhat met someone in the schoolyard and left with him of his own free will.

anchor.surface_text: 41.  The Government submitted that, according to various witnesses, on 28 July 1993 Ferhat had met someone in the schoolyard and had left with him of his own free will.

facts.text: The authorities tapped the anonymous telephone call on 4 August 1993; a raid at the address mentioned found empty premises; authorities concluded Ferhat's killing was the work of the PKK.

anchor.surface_text: 42.  The authorities, at the request of the applicant, tapped the anonymous telephone call on 4 August 1993. Although a raid was carried out at the address mentioned in the telephone conversation, the premises were found to be empty. The authorities of the Ministry of the Interior nevertheless established that the residence searched belonged to reporters from Özgür Gündem in Elazığ and concluded that Ferhat’s killing had been the work of the PKK.

facts.text: A report of 24 September 1993 from the Ministry of the Interior and a letter of 16 November 1995 from the governor of Bitlis indicate that Ferhat's death was the work of the PKK.

anchor.surface_text: 43.  A report of 24 September 1993 from the Ministry of the Interior to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a letter of 16 November 1995 from the governor of Bitlis province indicate that the death of the applicant’s son was the work of the PKK.

facts.text: The Chief Public Prosecutor of Elazığ informed the Ministry of Justice on 10 November 1995 that there was no indication or record of Ferhat having been taken into custody; custody records of Bitlis Security Directorate contained no mention of him.

anchor.surface_text: 44.  In a letter of 10 November 1995 the Chief Public Prosecutor of Elazığ, charged with investigating Ferhat Tepe’s death, informed the Ministry of Justice that there was no indication or record of Ferhat’s having been taken into custody. Moreover, the custody records of the Bitlis Security Directorate contained no mention of him.

facts.text: On 28 July 1993, two plain-clothes men made enquiries about Ferhat in the building where he lived; a witness told police officers about this on 29 July 1993.

anchor.surface_text: 55.  In this statement, the witness was asked to say what he knew about the incident. He replied that on 28 July 1993, at around 4 p.m., he had seen two plain-clothes men making enquiries about Ferhat. When one of them asked whether he knew Ferhat and the other residents of the building, the witness told them that Ferhat lived there and gave the names of the other residents.

facts.text: On 28 July 1993, at around 6.30 or 7 p.m., a witness saw Ferhat talking to two women and one or two men next to a bakery; a white Renault Toros with registration '65' was parked nearby with two young men inside.

anchor.surface_text: 57.  On 28 July 1993, at around 6.30 or 7 p.m., the witness saw Ferhat Tepe talking to two women and one or two men next to a bakery. A white Renault Toros with the registration number “65” attracted the witness’s attention as its parking lights were on. There were two young men in the car.

facts.text: On 28 July 1993, at about 7 or 7.30 p.m., Fatih Olcay saw a bearded man waiting in the schoolyard; Ferhat arrived and they left arm in arm like friends; no force was used.

anchor.surface_text: 58.  The witness was 17 years old at the relevant time. On 28 July 1993, at about 7 or 7.30 p.m., he was playing football with his friends in the Şemsi Bitlis primary school yard. He saw a bearded man aged about 20-25 waiting in the schoolyard. Two or three minutes later Ferhat arrived and they left the schoolyard arm in arm, like two friends. The bearded man did not use any force against Ferhat.

facts.text: The autopsy on 4 August 1993 found no signs of blows or use of force; cause of death was drowning; no systematic autopsy was deemed necessary.

anchor.surface_text: 50.  An autopsy was carried out on Ferhat’s body by the public prosecutor, a medical expert and the latter’s assistant in the presence of two witnesses and a clerk. It was observed that rigor mortis had not set in and the body had not yet turned blue, that water spurted out when the chest was pressed, that light violet-coloured cyanosis was perceptible on the ears and the nails of both the hands and the feet as a result of suffocation and that there were no signs of any blow or of the use of force on the body, nor were there any signs of friction on the hands and feet. It was therefore concluded that the cause of death was drowning and that there was no need for a systematic autopsy.

facts.text: Witnesses Mümtaz Çerçel, Ömer Aceban, Bahri Elçi, Miğdat Yaşar, Murat Koparan, Taner Şarlak, Erkan Dağdelen, Urfi Pasin and Rıza Demirtaş alleged Ferhat was held and tortured by security forces between 28 July and 4 August 1993.

anchor.surface_text: 27.  The applicant alleged that, according to the eyewitnesses Mümtaz Çerçel, Ömer Aceban, Bahri Elçi, Miğdat Yaşar, Murat Koparan, Taner Şarlak, Erkan Dağdelen, Urfi Pasin and Rıza Demirtaş, who had been apprehended and questioned at the relevant time in the Diyarbakır Recruitment Office, Ferhat had been held there and tortured by members of the security forces between 28 July and 4 August 1993.

The applicant’s daughter was remanded in custody in December 1993; his son was remanded in custody in 1994 for four months and is currently being tried for an offence which carries the death sentence; another of the applicant’s daughters was taken into custody in April 1994; four of the applicant’s nephews were remanded in custody in 1994, one of whom is being tried for an offence which carries the death sentence; the applicant’s brother was taken into custody in April 1994 and the applicant’s cousin has been in Elazığ Prison since 1994. On 24 February 1996 the applicant was arrested in Bartın and held in police custody for eight days in Bitlis. During his detention, the police officers asked him why he accused the State and why he had taken his complaints to the European Commission. They further threatened him and said among other things: “We will kill you just as we killed Ferhat. You are complaining to the infidels about our State. Are they the ones who will save you? Well, let them come and save you.” After being released, the applicant was acquitted of the charges by the Diyarbakır State Security Court. On 4 March 1996 the applicant was allegedly taken into custody in Bitlis on charges of aiding the PKK. He was released on an unspecified date after being interrogated.

arguments.claim: The applicant submitted that in 1999 he was arrested by anti-terrorist police while entering the HADEP party building in Istanbul, detained for one day, insulted and threatened with death by police officers.

anchor.surface_text: In 1999 the applicant was arrested by police officers from the anti-terrorist department while entering the HADEP (People’s Democracy Party) party building in the Kadıköy district in Istanbul. He was kept in detention for one day. The police officers insulted him and threatened him with death. One of the police officers said that they would kill him just as they had killed Ferhat. The applicant complained to the Fatih Public Prosecutor in Istanbul, who decided to discontinue the proceedings, as there was no witness to confirm his allegations.

arguments.claim: The Government submitted that Ferhat Tepe had been arrested twice in 1991 on suspicion of acting as a PKK courier.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant’s son Ferhat Tepe had been arrested on two occasions in 1991, as he was suspected of acting as a PKK courier.

arguments.claim: The Government submitted that, according to witnesses, on 28 July 1993 Ferhat met someone in the schoolyard and left with him of his own free will.

anchor.surface_text: The Government submitted that, according to various witnesses, on 28 July 1993 Ferhat had met someone in the schoolyard and had left with him of his own free will.

arguments.claim: The Government submitted that authorities tapped the anonymous telephone call on 4 August 1993; a raid at the address mentioned found empty premises; authorities concluded Ferhat's killing was the work of the PKK.

anchor.surface_text: The authorities, at the request of the applicant, tapped the anonymous telephone call on 4 August 1993. Although a raid was carried out at the address mentioned in the telephone conversation, the premises were found to be empty. The authorities of the Ministry of the Interior nevertheless established that the residence searched belonged to reporters from Özgür Gündem in Elazığ and concluded that Ferhat’s killing had been the work of the PKK.

arguments.claim: The Government submitted that reports from the Ministry of the Interior and the governor of Bitlis indicate that Ferhat's death was the work of the PKK.

anchor.surface_text: A report of 24 September 1993 from the Ministry of the Interior to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and a letter of 16 November 1995 from the governor of Bitlis province indicate that the death of the applicant’s son was the work of the PKK.

arguments.claim: The Government submitted that the Chief Public Prosecutor of Elazığ informed the Ministry of Justice that there was no indication or record of Ferhat having been taken into custody; custody records contained no mention of him.

anchor.surface_text: In a letter of 10 November 1995 the Chief Public Prosecutor of Elazığ, charged with investigating Ferhat Tepe’s death, informed the Ministry of Justice that there was no indication or record of Ferhat’s having been taken into custody. Moreover, the custody records of the Bitlis Security Directorate contained no mention of him.

anchor.surface_text: The Court, having regard to the factual dispute between the parties over the circumstances surrounding the death of the applicant’s son, conducted an investigation pursuant to Article 38 § 1 (a) of the Convention.
